per_case.playbook: 1) Immediately isolate WEB-BO-01 from the network (disable network access but preserve forensic state). 2) Block source IP 185.220.101.4 at the edge firewall. 3) Reset the 'deploy' account password and audit all credentials that accessed the host. 4) Conduct full forensic imaging and malware analysis to identify persistence mechanisms. 5) Check for lateral movement to other hosts (same source IP, deploy user, or sudo activity). 6) Rebuild host from known-good image rather than cleaning in place, given root-level compromise.

Immediately isolate FILE-BO-01 from the network (disable network access via switch port / VLAN quarantine). Preserve the host for forensic analysis before rebuilding. Reset credentials for the 'svc_backup' account and any other accounts it can access. Block external IP 91.240.118.172 at the perimeter firewall and add to threat intel watchlist. Investigate the source of the brute-force (likely lateral movement from another internal host) and hunt for the staged archive 'fin.7z' and any exfiltration. Review backup integrity since volume shadows were deleted.

1) Immediately isolate WS-NKAPOOR-01 from the network (disable network access via switch port or EDR isolation). 2) Preserve forensic images (memory dump + disk) before remediation. 3) Block outbound connections to 45.83.221.30 at the firewall and add to DNS/URL filtering. 4) Investigate the triggering process chain (wmiprvse.exe -> powershell.exe, PID 7304, PPID 1988) and hunt for the dropped payload. 5) Reset credentials for NORTHSTAR\nkapoor and review for lateral movement. 6) Hunt across the fleet for the same PowerShell signature and beaconing pattern. 7) Open an incident ticket and escalate to IR per the malware response playbook.

No action required. Close as a false positive / benign. No need to isolate the host or block any IP. If alerting on this host continues, review the alert source for false-positive tuning; the failed-then-successful logon is consistent with a user mistyping their password.

BLOCK_IP — Add 45.83.220.5 to the perimeter firewall deny list / IPS block list immediately. Confirm the scan was fully blocked (firewall logs already show denies). Verify WEB-BO-01 has no successful /phpmyadmin access or follow-up exploitation by reviewing subsequent web access logs. No host isolation required since there is no confirmed compromise. Monitor for additional scan sources and report to IR if the IP is associated with a broader campaign.

1) Isolate host 10.20.3.44 from the network immediately to halt the C2 beacon. 2) Preserve forensic images and capture memory for malware analysis. 3) Block egress to 45.83.221.30 at the firewall and add to threat intel blocklist. 4) Identify the initial access vector and perform full endpoint malware scan. 5) Hunt for lateral movement or persistence from 10.20.3.44 across the environment. 6) Rebuild the host from known-good image after eradication.

Block external IP 198.51.100.77 at the edge firewall. Review VPN account vhales for any successful authentication or suspicious activity. Monitor for additional failed login attempts or credential-stuffing patterns. Escalate to incident response if further attempts indicate a brute-force or unauthorized access campaign.

Immediately isolate DC-BO-01 from the network (disable network access via switch port / firewall block, but preserve volatile memory for forensics). Trigger incident response for a domain controller compromise: (1) assume full domain credential compromise — force immediate password reset for all accounts, especially jbiros and high-privilege service accounts; (2) hunt for DCSync/lateral movement from source 10.20.3.70 and other hosts; (3) preserve disk image and memory dump of DC-BO-01 for forensics; (4) remove the Mimikatz binary C:\Users\Public\m.exe and investigate how it was dropped; (5) review all domain trust relationships and consider rotating domain admin / KRBTGT hashes; (6) escalate to the IR/forensics team as a critical-severity domain compromise.

1) Isolate SQL-BO-01 from the network immediately to prevent lateral movement. 2) Disable/delete the newly created 'svc_sql' account and rotate all credentials, especially SQL 'sa' and svc_sql service accounts. 3) Preserve forensic images/logs before remediation. 4) Investigate the source host 10.20.3.62 for compromise and check 10.20.2.30 for lateral movement. 5) Patch/audit SQL Server xp_cmdshell configuration and review for other persistence mechanisms.

Immediately isolate WS-LCHEN-01 from the network. Preserve the host for forensic analysis (capture memory, PowerShell transcript, and the downloaded update.bin). Block the external IP 193.32.162.44 and domain cdn-update-center.net at the perimeter. Investigate the originating Word document and the account NORTHSTAR\lchen for initial access vector. Check for additional lateral movement or persistence from this host.

Isolate MAIL-BO-01 from the network immediately. Investigate the postfix/smtp process (PID 3321) for compromise or backdoor. Block outbound SMTP to 45.155.205.233 and the mx01.example.net hostname at the firewall. Capture memory and disk images for forensics. Review mail queue and logs for the source of automated mail generation. Rotate credentials for any accounts associated with the mail server. Once contained, determine the initial access vector and scope of exfiltrated data.

Immediately isolate BKUP-BO-01 from the network. Disable the 'svc_upd' account and remove it from Administrators. Preserve the host for forensic analysis, then remove the malicious scheduled task '\Updater\SysSync' and delete C:\Windows\Temp\sync.exe. Hunt for lateral movement from the compromised service account and review other hosts that interacted with BKUP-BO-01. Rotate credentials for svc_upd and any accounts it had access to.

Immediately isolate WS-JDIAZ-01 from the network. Preserve the lsass.dmp dump and the svc.exe binary for forensic analysis. Reset credentials for the NORTHSTAR\jdiaz account and any privileged accounts it may have accessed. Hunt for lateral movement using the compromised credentials. Launch EDR on the host to identify the implant, enumerate persistence mechanisms, and capture the parent process lineage. Initiate full incident response per credential-theft playbook.

Immediately isolate APP-BO-02 from the network (disable switch port / move to quarantine VLAN). Preserve the host's memory and disk forensically before remediation. Block outbound traffic to 45.83.221.30 (all ports) and the associated ports 4444/8080 at the perimeter firewall. Rotate credentials for the 'ubuntu' account and any other accounts that accessed the host. Conduct full malware analysis of the downloaded lin.sh and hunt for persistence mechanisms and lateral movement to peers. Rebuild the host from known-good image after eradicating the threat.

Block IP 185.220.101.4 at the edge firewall (add permanent deny rule for the outside interface). Verify WEB-BO-02 / 10.20.1.11 has no successful root SSH login from this IP via auth logs. Confirm SSH is not exposed to the internet where possible; enforce key-based auth and fail2ban. Monitor for follow-up attacks from adjacent IPs in the 185.220.101.0/24 range.

1) Block source IP 103.152.90.14 at the edge firewall/IPS immediately. 2) Verify the WAF/IDS rules are active for the web tier. 3) Confirm whether the SQL injection succeeded by reviewing application logs and DB integrity on WEB-BO-02 — if any injection succeeded, escalate to ISOLATE_HOST and initiate credential rotation. 4) Ensure parameterized queries/prepared statements are in place for the /api/claims endpoint. 5) Monitor for follow-up attacks from associated infrastructure.

Immediately isolate WEB-BO-02 (10.20.1.11) from the network to contain the webshell threat. Preserve forensic images/logs before remediation. Remove the uploaded webshell file (shell.php) and any additional planted files. Investigate the host for additional persistence, backdoors, and lateral movement to other internal systems. Rotate credentials for any accounts or services accessible from the web server. Block the source IP 194.26.29.88 at the edge firewall as a secondary measure. Review the web application for the underlying file-upload vulnerability and patch it before returning the host to production.

Block source IP 91.240.118.172 at the edge firewall/IDS immediately. Verify FILE-BO-01 and 10.20.2.20 have no successful RDP logons from this IP. Force a password reset for the 'administrator' account as a precaution, enforce MFA and RDP account lockout policies, and review firewall logs for any other connections from this IP. Continue monitoring for follow-up attempts from associated infrastructure.

Isolate host 10.20.3.62 from the network immediately. Preserve the network session (uid C19m1) and perform forensic imaging. Block/allow-list the external IP 193.32.162.44 and domain cdn-update-center.net at the edge firewall. Hunt for lateral movement and Emotet IOCs across the fleet, then remediate and rebuild the compromised host.

Block source IP 80.94.95.226 at the edge firewall. Add persistent deny rules for inbound connections from this IP. Monitor for continued scanning activity and correlate against threat intelligence once the reputation service is restored.

Block external IP 222.186.42.7 at the edge firewall immediately. Force a password reset for user 'amorgan' and verify account lockout policies are engaging. Review WS-AMORGAN-01 and 10.20.3.91 for any residual activity, and confirm RDP is not exposed to the internet. Monitor for continued attempts from related ranges.

No action required. Close as benign/low-priority noise. Confirm 40.97.128.10 is within the expected Microsoft 365 service IP range and ensure it is on the allowlist. No need to isolate host or block IP.

No action required. Confirm with the backup team that 10.20.4.15 is an authorized backup source and that the hourly 40MB transfers match the expected backup schedule. If the cadence or volume ever changes unexpectedly, re-evaluate. No blocking or isolation needed.

No action required. Close as benign/false positive. Confirm the alert was triggered by routine Windows Update (wuauclt.exe/wuauserv) activity. No host isolation or IP blocking needed. Monitor for any subsequent anomalous process activity on the host, but no immediate remediation is warranted.

Close as false positive. No action required. Optionally tune the IDS signature to whitelist the internal Nessus scanner IP (10.20.0.40) to suppress recurring 'Nessus User-Agent' noise from scheduled scans.

No action required. This appears to be a false positive or misrouted alert. Confirm the alert source and verify it is not a duplicate/misconfigured sensor. Continue routine monitoring of WEB-BO-02; no isolation or blocking is warranted given the absence of any malicious evidence.
No action required. Dismiss the alert as a false positive. Confirm DNS-BO-01 is operating normally as a DNS resolver. No host isolation or IP block needed.

No action required at this time. Recommend verifying the alert source and confirming whether '203.0.113.77' is a valid target in scope. If the alert is confirmed legitimate, ensure the relevant sensor/telemetry pipeline is ingesting data into the triage database. Re-run this triage once data is available. Monitor for any future activity from this IP across all tables.
No action required. Close the alert as a false positive / benign activity. Continue standard monitoring; no host isolation or IP block recommended.

No action required. This is benign internal file-sharing activity. Confirm mtaylor is an authorized finance user and FILE-BO-01 is a sanctioned file server; if confirmed, close the alert as a false positive and continue monitoring.

Isolate WS-KORAM-01 from the network immediately. Disable/reset the NORTHSTAR\koram account credentials and review for any lateral movement or suspicious activity performed under that account. Preserve the host for forensic analysis and verify the legitimacy of the TEAMS.EXE process launch. Rotate credentials for any accounts that shared access to this host.
